title: Playing presidential inaugural balls from Roosevelt to Carter
summary: Leeman recalls six inaugural balls starting with Roosevelt's in 1940 with Barnet, Nixon's with Condon's band, and Carter's in 1977, and the Marine trumpeters taking over ruffles and flourishes.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: I might add that while I'm thinking of it, that in 1977, I played the inauguration ball for President Carter in Washington, D.C. with the World's Greatest Jazz Band.

And that was my sixth Presidential Ball, beginning with FDR Roosevelt's in 1940, I believe that was the first one I did with Charlie Barnet , and I did one after that, another, which of course was Roosevelt, with Charlie Barnet , which was a repeat inaugural, and I made them all with the exception, I guess, of -- I did make them all with the exception of Lyndon Johnson, who of course, had no inaugural ball because he was sworn in upon the death of President Jack Kennedy.

I played another Presidential ball, which is a story we must cover if we ever have time, but right now I'll just mention it was the inaugural ball for Richard Nixon, with Eddie Condon's six-piece jazz orchestra, and we had Wild Bill Davison on trumpet and Lou Stein on piano, and Jack Lesberg on bass, and I must tell the story at some other point, it was a motley crew -- please believe me.

It was white tie and tails, for one thing, and we had business suits on, which all in all, was casual. In the second place, we're standing there and Condon said, "When he comes out, do we play ruffles and flourishes?" and Wild Bill took a drink and says, "I don't know" and there came a soft voice behind Eddie Condon, and the head of the Marine Presidential greeting trumpets said, "No, we'll play that!"
